title: Season-dependent activity slopes retain the known 13.5-day HD 1461 velocity signal in selected HARPS and HIRES data
abstract: We test whether changing linear activity responses remove the known HD 1461 velocity wave. We use 244 HARPS nights and 214 independent HIRES nights. Three HARPS diagnostics and the HIRES calcium index have global or seasonal velocity slopes. Seasonal fits retain amplitudes of 1.431 and 1.565 m/s. The fixed HARPS wave reduces HIRES weighted error by 18.60 percent. A conditional 30-day block interval is 8.84 to 30.65 percent. Removal of each season leaves a gain of 16.07 to 22.41 percent. The fits retain at least 83 and 92 percent of target wave information. The result limits the tested linear activity explanations. It does not exclude nonlinear stellar activity, prove an orbit or find a new planet. Intervals hold the training wave fixed. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, retrieval steps and a figure are included. External source records are excluded.
